CobolAnalyzer.observations: The prompt establishes scope (128 programs, 387 copybooks, 206K lines) and requests the right analytical categories (SQL, file I/O, CALLs, copybooks, SORT, calculations). The representative code samples are genuinely useful — T660DO10.cpy reveals a massive COMMAREA-style copybook (109,640 bytes) with multilevel REDEFINES, multiple INDEXED BY clauses, and multilingual arrays; KYGHR002.cbl shows embedded DB2 SQL with SQLCA error handling, European decimal notation (DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA), and a layered PERFORM-based business logic pattern. However, the prompt misses several codebase-specific patterns that would directly cause conversion errors: (1) no target language specified — Java, C#, and Python require fundamentally different struct/class mappings for REDEFINES; (2) no instruction to capture COMP/COMP-3/COMP-4 binary vs. packed-decimal distinctions which are lossy when naively mapped to floats; (3) GEN-AREA/COMMAREA framework pattern (IDUSER, IDBA, KDBEHAND, KDRETUR with codes 000/001/002/003) is a pervasive cross-program contract not identified; (4) DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA in KYGHR002 is a critical numeric format difference not flagged; (5) Swedish/Spanish mixed-language field naming conventions (KD=code, ID=identifier, FL=flag, BE=description, TI=timestamp) need a glossary to preserve semantics; (6) 88-level condition names as business rules (DB2-OK, MIGRADO-SI, TRATAR-AMBAS-SI) are not called out as a pattern requiring explicit mapping; (7) large FILLER OCCURS blocks (up to 2000 bytes) indicating reserved expansion areas need a modernization decision; (8) the modification log markers (L-0001 through L-0016) encode active business rule evolution that is invisible to the output structure requested; (9) no mention of EBCDIC/encoding concerns for the Swedish special characters already corrupted in the sample.
